objectives.en: I can talk about rules and obligations with must and have to.

warmup.en: Think about your school, a club or a job you know. What do you have to do there? What isn't allowed? What isn't necessary? Make a quick list in English or Hebrew.
warmup.he: חשבו על בית הספר שלכם, על חוג או על מקום עבודה שאתם מכירים: מה חייבים לעשות שם? מה אסור? ומה לא חובה? בעברית יש לנו 'חייבים', 'אסור' ו'לא חייבים'. היום נלמד את שלושתם באנגלית – וגם איך לתת עצה.

explanation.en: Lior has a new job at a café. He has to wear a black T-shirt. He must be on time. He mustn't use his phone behind the counter. He doesn't have to work on Saturdays. His manager's advice: 'You should ask a lot of questions in your first week.'
explanation.he: ליאור התחיל לעבוד בבית קפה. הוא חייב ללבוש חולצה שחורה (has to), הוא חייב להגיע בזמן (must), אסור לו להשתמש בטלפון מאחורי הדלפק (mustn't), והוא לא חייב לעבוד בשבת (doesn't have to). העצה של המנהלת: 'כדאי לך לשאול הרבה שאלות בשבוע הראשון' (should).

rows: You must wear a seat belt. I have to work tomorrow.

explanation.en: mustn't and don't have to are NOT the same. You mustn't park here = it's not allowed. You don't have to park here = it's not necessary, but you can if you want.
explanation.he: mustn't ו-don't have to הם לא אותו דבר! You mustn't park here – אסור לחנות כאן. You don't have to park here – לא חייבים לחנות כאן, אבל מותר אם רוצים.

explanation.en: must, mustn't, should and shouldn't + base verb, with no to and no -s: She must go (not *She must to go or *She musts go). have to changes like a normal verb: I have to, she has to, Do you have to ...?, She doesn't have to ...
explanation.he: אחרי must, mustn't, should ו-shouldn't בא פועל בסיס, בלי to ובלי s: She must go (ולא She must to go או She musts go). לעומת זאת, have to משתנה כמו פועל רגיל: I have to, she has to, Do you have to ...?, She doesn't have to ...

explanation.en: In positive sentences, must and have to are very close. must is common in written rules and signs (Visitors must sign in); in conversation, have to is more common. For the past, use had to: I had to wait an hour.
explanation.he: במשפט חיובי must ו-have to כמעט זהים. must נפוץ בחוקים כתובים ובשלטים (Visitors must sign in), ובשיחה יומיומית have to נפוץ יותר. בעבר משתמשים ב-had to: I had to wait an hour.

explanation.en: Make advice softer with I think or I don't think: I think you should rest. I don't think you should go.
explanation.he: אפשר לרכך עצה בעזרת I think או I don't think: I think you should rest. I don't think you should go.

hebrew_pitfalls.en: In Hebrew a question like 'do I have to pay?' keeps statement word order with no helper verb, so it is easy to say *I have to pay? English needs do or does: Do I have to pay? Does she have to work on Friday?
hebrew_pitfalls.he: בעברית שואלים 'אני צריך לשלם?' בלי פועל עזר, ולכן קל לומר I have to pay?. באנגלית צריך do או does: Do I have to pay? Does she have to work on Friday?

hebrew_pitfalls.en: Hebrew present-tense verbs change for gender and number, not for person (I have to and he has to are the same Hebrew verb form). So the English he/she/it form is easy to miss: she has to (not *she have to). Modals never change: she must, he should (not *she musts).
hebrew_pitfalls.he: בהווה בעברית הפועל משתנה לפי מין ומספר, אבל לא לפי גוף: 'אני צריך' ו'הוא צריך' – אותה צורה. לכן קל לשכוח את הצורה המיוחדת של he/she/it באנגלית: she has to (ולא she have to). לעומת זאת must ו-should לא משתנים לעולם: she must, he should (ולא she musts).

hebrew_pitfalls.en: In Hebrew there is one 'u' vowel, so should /ʃʊd/ can come out long, like 'shood'. Keep it short, as in good and book, and don't say the l.
hebrew_pitfalls.he: בעברית יש תנועת 'u' אחת, ולכן should /ʃʊd/ עלול לצאת ארוך, כמו 'שוּוּד'. אמרו אותו קצר, כמו ב-good וב-book, ובלי לבטא את ה-l.

explanation.en: have to = necessary · mustn't = not allowed · don't have to = not necessary · should = a good idea · shouldn't = a bad idea · can = allowed.
explanation.he: have to = חייבים · mustn't = אסור · don't have to = לא חייבים · should = כדאי · shouldn't = לא כדאי · can = מותר.

prompt.en: Read the sign and choose what it means.

exercises.question: A sign in a museum: NO PHOTOS
options: You don't have to take photos.

0.en: don't have to = it's not necessary, but it's OK. The sign says it's not allowed: mustn't.
0.he: don't have to פירושו 'לא חייבים' – אבל מותר. השלט אומר שאסור: mustn't.

2.en: should is advice. A NO sign is a rule: you mustn't.
2.he: should היא עצה. שלט עם NO הוא חוק: mustn't.

3.en: This means the opposite. NO PHOTOS = taking photos is not allowed.
3.he: זה ההפך. NO PHOTOS פירושו שאסור לצלם.

explanation.en: NO + something on a sign = you mustn't do it.
explanation.he: שלט עם NO פירושו שאסור לעשות את הדבר: you mustn't.

0.en: 'You don't have to bring food' – it's not necessary, because there's a café.
0.he: 'You don't have to bring food' – לא צריך להביא אוכל, כי יש בית קפה.

2.en: Listen again: one thing is necessary.
2.he: הקשיבו שוב: יש דבר אחד שחובה להביא.

explanation.en: 'You must bring your student card' = it's necessary. 'You don't have to bring food' = it's not necessary.
explanation.he: 'You must bring your student card' – חובה. 'You don't have to bring food' – לא חובה.

prompt.en: Necessary, not allowed or not necessary? Sort the sentences.

explanation.en: must / have to → necessary · mustn't / can't → not allowed · don't have to / doesn't have to → not necessary.
explanation.he: must / have to → חובה · mustn't / can't → אסור · don't have to / doesn't have to → לא חובה.

exercises.question: Tomorrow is a holiday, so we ___ go to school.

0.en: mustn't means it's not allowed. Going to school isn't forbidden – it just isn't necessary: don't have to.
0.he: mustn't פירושו 'אסור'. ללכת לבית הספר זה לא אסור – פשוט לא צריך: don't have to.

1.en: shouldn't is advice (a bad idea). Here it's about what is necessary.
1.he: shouldn't היא עצה ('לא כדאי'). כאן מדובר על מה שחובה או לא חובה.

feedback.he: לכבות את הטלפון זה רעיון טוב, ולכן: You should switch it off.

explanation.en: should = a good idea · shouldn't = a bad idea. Both are followed by the base verb: shouldn't go, should switch.

exercises.title: Your first day at Shell Beach Café
exercises.passage:
Hi Omer,
Welcome to the team! Here are a few things you need to know before Sunday.
You have to be here at 7:30, half an hour before we open. You don't have to bring a uniform – we'll give you two T-shirts – but you must wear black trousers and comfortable shoes.
Staff mustn't use their phones behind the counter, but you can check them on your break. You don't have to pay for coffee or lunch during your shift.
One more thing: the first week is always busy, so you should drink a lot of water, and you shouldn't stay up late on Saturday night!
See you soon,
Rachel

prompt.en: Write a message with rules and advice.

task.en: A student from abroad is joining your school, course or workplace next week. Write them a message (50-80 words). Include two things they have to / must do, one thing they mustn't do, one thing they don't have to do, and two pieces of advice with should or shouldn't.
task.he: תלמיד או תלמידה מחו״ל מצטרפים בשבוע הבא לבית הספר, לקורס או למקום העבודה שלכם. כתבו להם הודעה (50-80 מילים). כללו שני דברים שחייבים לעשות (have to / must), דבר אחד שאסור (mustn't), דבר אחד שלא חייבים (don't have to), ושתי עצות עם should או shouldn't.

exercises.model_answer: Hi Priya! I'm so happy you're joining our school. You have to wear the school T-shirt every day, and you must be in class by 8:15. You mustn't use your phone during lessons – the teachers are very strict about that. You don't have to bring lunch, because there's a cafeteria. You should bring a water bottle, because it's hot here, and you shouldn't sit at the back if you want to hear the teacher. See you on Sunday!

checklist.en: I used have to or must for two things that are necessary.
checklist.he: השתמשתי ב-have to או ב-must לשני דברים שחובה לעשות.

checklist.en: I used mustn't for something not allowed and don't have to for something not necessary – not the other way round.
checklist.he: השתמשתי ב-mustn't למשהו אסור וב-don't have to למשהו שלא חובה – ולא להפך.

checklist.en: After must, mustn't, should and shouldn't, I used the base verb with no to.
checklist.he: אחרי must, mustn't, should ו-shouldn't השתמשתי בפועל בסיס, בלי to.

checklist.en: I gave two pieces of advice with should or shouldn't.
checklist.he: נתתי שתי עצות עם should או shouldn't.

key_points.en: must / have to = necessary. She has to ... Do you have to ...?
key_points.he: must / have to = חובה. She has to ... Do you have to ...?

key_points.en: mustn't = not allowed. don't have to = not necessary. They are NOT the same.
key_points.he: mustn't = אסור. don't have to = לא חובה. הם לא אותו דבר!

key_points.en: should / shouldn't = advice: You should rest. You shouldn't worry.
key_points.he: should / shouldn't = עצה: You should rest. You shouldn't worry.

key_points.en: Modal + base verb, with no to and no -s: She must go. He should call.
key_points.he: פועל מודאלי + פועל בסיס, בלי to ובלי s: She must go. He should call.

key_points.en: The past of must / have to is had to: I had to wait.
key_points.he: העבר של must ושל have to הוא had to: I had to wait.
